guard: The engine seam enforces the same laws the walker enforces inline: the member laws (L4014/L4018/L4020), freeze-on-share in both halves (L2031/L2032), the fuel budget and its macrotask yield (L4013 + the cut), the thenable gate the walker cannot survive, the calling-convention adapter that exists only on this side (and ruling 1c's invariant that it is invisible from inside the program), and the host's run wiring (source-pinned hash, the resume refusals, the run-bound effect ceiling). (FAIL-FAST suite: markers are upstream of the cells they guard.)
why: These cells are first-party rather than differential, because the walker cannot grade them: the
fuel unit changes in languageVersion 2, the thenable programs kill the walker's host process, and
the calling-convention adapter has no walker counterpart. A first-party cell with no mutant is a
cell nobody has shown can fail, so every law the seam claims to hold gets a mutation here.
ONE CELL HERE HAS NO MUTANT, ON PURPOSE. `the library calls exactly the argument positions the
seam adapts` is a drift alarm on library.ts, which this lane may not edit: it probes every name in
every table with a marker and compares the positions the library ACTUALLY calls to the ones the
seam adapts. It is declaration-independent by construction, so mutating the seam's list cannot red
it - the two mutants that grade that list are the ones on `adaptArgs` and on the read form. Its own
failure mode, finding nothing at all, is graded by the count cell beside it.

mutations.name: a record answers the host prototype for a name it does not own
mutations.find: return Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(obj, prop) ? (obj as Record<string, unknown>)[prop] : undefined;
mutations.expectRed: a record answers undefined for `constructor`
mutations.completionMarker: ok a record answers its own field
mutations.cell: a record answers undefined for `constructor`
mutations.note: The walker's own member-access mutation guards this hole on its side. The engine reaches records through a different door, so the hole has to be closed and graded twice; it is not covered by the walker's config.

mutations.name: a method is handed out as a value instead of being resolved at the call
mutations.expectRed: a method read as a VALUE is L4020, not a bound function
mutations.completionMarker: ok and a name outside that table is L4014
mutations.cell: a method read as a VALUE is L4020, not a bound function
mutations.note: Handing one out produces everything a bound-function factory produces: `xs.map !== xs.map` where JavaScript says equal, and an extracted `push` that writes to a receiver strict JavaScript refuses.

mutations.name: the birth-depth check is dropped, so a value born outside a branch is writable inside it
mutations.expectRed: a value born outside a concurrent branch and written inside it is L2032
mutations.completionMarker: ok a value that crossed an effect boundary is frozen and refuses a write (L2031)
mutations.cell: a value born outside a concurrent branch and written inside it is L2032
mutations.note: L2032's runtime half, reached through a VALUE rather than a binding. The static walk provably cannot see the alias path, so this door is the only one on it.

mutations.name: the thenable gate at birth is dropped
mutations.expectRed: a literal with an own callable `then` refuses at birth
mutations.completionMarker: ok writing a member of null is L4010
mutations.cell: a literal with an own callable `then` refuses at birth
mutations.note: Measured: returning such a value out of any async function runs its `then` with the host's settlement functions as arguments, outside the run's frame. Birth is one of the two doors that close the whole value graph. The cell captures the outcome instead of returning the value through its own async boundary: written the other way, this mutant made the suite HANG rather than fail (the assimilated `then` ignores resolve, so the promise never settles, exit 13) — the hazard demonstrating itself inside the cell meant to grade it.

mutations.name: the thenable gate at a field write is dropped, so a record acquires one after birth
mutations.find: if (prop === "then") refuseThenable({ then: v }, "this field write");
mutations.expectRed: writing a callable into the field `then` refuses (L4018)
mutations.completionMarker: ok a FUNCTION carrying an own callable `then` refuses at birth too
mutations.cell: writing a callable into the field `then` refuses (L4018)
mutations.note: The second door. Without it `x["th" + "en"] = f` mints the hazard past any static spelling of the name, which is the shape no emitter-side check can see.

mutations.name: the thenable gate at await is dropped, so the host calls the closure first
mutations.expectRed: awaiting an own-callable-`then` value is L4018
mutations.completionMarker: ok writing a NON-callable into `then` stays legal
mutations.cell: awaiting an own-callable-`then` value is L4018
mutations.note: The cell's second conjunct is what this mutant really exposes: the gate has to run BEFORE the await, because once `await` has the value the host has already called its `then`.

mutations.name: the step budget never fires
mutations.expectRed: the step budget fires as L4013
mutations.completionMarker: ok and a plain value awaits to itself
mutations.cell: the step budget fires as L4013
mutations.note: The effect ceiling is blind to a loop that performs nothing, by construction. This is the only bound on pure work, and a later cell in this suite relies on it to end a soft-cancelled spin, so under this mutant the suite would hang if the graded cell did not red first.

mutations.name: fuel never yields, so the macrotask queue is starved
mutations.expectRed: with yielding on, a host macrotask timer fires DURING the run
mutations.completionMarker: ok and it fires AT the budget rather than after it
mutations.cell: with yielding on, a host macrotask timer fires DURING the run
mutations.note: A program that only ever yields microtasks takes the host down with it: a watchdog's setTimeout never fires, and the run kills the timer plane and every other run on that host. The cell is a PAIR, so this mutant reddens the claim while its control still passes.

mutations.name: the yield boundary ignores the cut
mutations.expectRed: a branch cut at the pure level is abandoned at its next yield
mutations.completionMarker: ok and the control proves the cell can fail: with yielding off, it does not
mutations.cell: a branch cut at the pure level is abandoned at its next yield
mutations.note: The cut is the scope's call, not the yield's: an arm that cannot win is abandoned here, an arm that could still win runs its pure work to a settle. The cell beside this one grades the other arm of the same rule.

mutations.name: an own-field function is adapted as if it spoke the walker's convention
mutations.replace: answer = await (found.value as unknown as Callable)(currentFrame(), adaptArgs(found.key, list));
mutations.expectRed: and a member call through the seam agrees
mutations.completionMarker: ok a record-shaped builtin hands out program-convention members
mutations.cell: and a member call through the seam agrees
mutations.note: This is the defect the cell was written from, not one invented for the config: collapsing the table path and the own-field path adapted twice, passed the frame in as the first argument, and shifted every real argument along by a position — `json.stringify([1,2])` refused its own array as an illegal second argument, a convention mismatch wearing a coercion error's name.

mutations.name: a seam call with no frame invents one instead of failing
mutations.expectRed: a seam call outside any frame throws rather than inventing a root frame
mutations.completionMarker: ok calling a non-function value is L4011
mutations.cell: a seam call outside any frame throws rather than inventing a root frame
mutations.note: No fallback frame, deliberately: a stray call given a root frame gets a key namespace, a clock and a depth belonging to no branch, and its step lands in the wrong place in the journal instead of failing.

mutations.name: the run is pinned to the MODULE's hash instead of the source's
mutations.expectRed: its programHash is the SOURCE's hash, not the module's
mutations.completionMarker: ok runOnEngine answers the walker's RunResult shape
mutations.cell: its programHash is the SOURCE's hash, not the module's
mutations.note: A run record names the program an author wrote, not the string a compiler produced. Pinned to the module, a transform release would re-hash every open run and no walker-written journal could ever be resumed on the engine.

mutations.name: the source is never validated, so the engine executes what the walker would refuse
mutations.expectRed: invalid source is refused by the VALIDATOR
mutations.completionMarker: ok the step COUNTS differ, which is the declared v2 pin-unit divergence
mutations.cell: invalid source is refused by the VALIDATOR
mutations.note: The validator's refusals have to arrive before anything is journalled, whichever engine is about to execute; without this the engine is a second, laxer front door onto the same journal. This mutant SURVIVED the cell's first form, which only asserted that something threw - with `validate` gone the program still threw, because its module performs an unscripted effect. The cell now asserts the refusal is a LangErrors AND that the evaluator was never called.

mutations.name: a resume with no pins re-resolves them instead of refusing
mutations.expectRed: a journal with entries and no pins is L5021, not a silently different run
mutations.completionMarker: ok the caller's evaluator is what turns the module into a factory
mutations.cell: a journal with entries and no pins is L5021, not a silently different run
mutations.note: Silent by construction: the clock moves to the resuming host and the seed falls back to the runId default, and neither the epoch nor a pure draw is a recorded fact a replay could diverge on.

mutations.name: a run accepts another run's journal
mutations.expectRed: and another run's journal is L5011
mutations.completionMarker: ok a journal with entries and no pins is L5021, not a silently different run
mutations.cell: and another run's journal is L5011
mutations.note: Request ids derive from the runId while recorded results come from the journal, so a mismatch submits work under one identity and resolves it against another's history.

mutations.name: the effect ceiling counts per activation instead of per run
mutations.expectRed: a RESUMED run reaches the ceiling the RUN was pinned to, not a fresh one
mutations.completionMarker: ok a run right up to its ceiling completes
mutations.cell: a RESUMED run reaches the ceiling the RUN was pinned to, not a fresh one
mutations.note: The engine builds its own EffectHost, so this seeding is engine-specific wiring the walker's effect-ceiling config does not reach. Under the mutant the resume gets a full fresh allowance, performs the two remaining sleeps and ends GREEN with six entries - a runaway loop that crashes periodically never reaches the ceiling at all.

mutations.name: a builtin read as a VALUE does not adapt the callback it is handed
mutations.find: const p = async (...args: unknown[]): Promise<unknown> => await (v as Callable)(currentFrame(), adaptArgs(key, args));
mutations.replace: const p = async (...args: unknown[]): Promise<unknown> => await (v as Callable)(currentFrame(), args);
mutations.expectRed: a builtin read as a VALUE adapts the callback it is handed
mutations.completionMarker: ok so the run's frame never reaches the program through an element call
mutations.cell: a builtin read as a VALUE adapts the callback it is handed
mutations.note: The read form and the call form reach library.ts by different paths, and only one of them adapted. Reduced by lane T on the differential corpus: `const f = map; f([1, 2], (x) => x)` answered `[<EngineFrame>, <EngineFrame>]` - the run's own key scope, clock and cancellation signal handed to the program as an argument, readable and writable.

mutations.name: a builtin's program view is minted afresh on every read
mutations.find:
const had = programView.get(v as object);
    if (had !== undefined) return had;
mutations.expectRed: a builtin read twice is the same value
mutations.completionMarker: ok and the run's frame never reaches the program through it
mutations.cell: a builtin read twice is the same value
mutations.note: A builtin is ONE immutable binding for the whole run, so `map === map` is true on the walker. A fresh adapter per read makes it false, and nothing in the output of a program differs until it compares two reads.

mutations.name: every function in an argument list is adapted, not only the one the library calls
mutations.replace: return args.map((a) => (typeof a === "function" ? toWalker(a as (...x: unknown[]) => unknown) : a));
mutations.expectRed: a program closure stored through a library method reads back as the SAME value
mutations.completionMarker: ok and a member call through the seam agrees
mutations.cell: a program closure stored through a library method reads back as the SAME value
mutations.note: Ruling 1c's invariant, and the shape of the defect that produced it: a mutating method STORES its argument, so blanket adaptation put the walker view in the program's own array. Reduced by lane T - the program read it back and it neither called (`args is not iterable`) nor compared `===` to the value it pushed.

mutations.name: a member is classified by what it answered instead of by its name
mutations.replace:
const v = memberOf(obj, prop, asCallee);
    return typeof v === "function" ? { from: "table", fn: v as Callable, key: `${kind}.${prop}` } : { from: "own", value: v };
mutations.expectRed: a function ELEMENT is called as a program closure, not as a curated method
mutations.completionMarker: ok a program closure stored through a library method reads back as the SAME value
mutations.cell: a function ELEMENT is called as a program closure, not as a curated method
mutations.note: The second frame-leak door, found while writing the cell for the first and reproduced before the fix: an array element that happens to be a closure looked like a curated method, so `fs[0]("a")` was called `(frame, ["a"])` and ANSWERED the EngineFrame. Reads right, and wrong - the name decides the path, never the value the name produced.

mutations.name: free() does not serve the pure primitives or the event constructors
mutations.replace: if (name === "") freeNames.set(name, ((_frame, a) => impl(a)) as Callable);
mutations.expectRed: free() serves the pure primitives and the event constructors
mutations.completionMarker: ok the step COUNTS differ, which is the declared v2 pin-unit divergence
mutations.cell: free() serves the pure primitives and the event constructors
mutations.note: Ratified design 3A puts `channel`, `run`, `replied`, `message`, `idle` and `down` behind `free()`; the engine answered L2001 for all six, found by lane T's first differential run. The graded cell compares the SHAPES the two engines produce, so serving them from a second copy of the table would fail it just as serving nothing does.

mutations.name: the operand of `++` is not required to be a number
mutations.expectRed: a STRING operand of `++` refuses (L4018) rather than counting
mutations.completionMarker: ok unary `update` answers a number operand unchanged
mutations.cell: a STRING operand of `++` refuses (L4018) rather than counting
mutations.note: Ruled in 1c: the walker reads the operand through `Number(...)`, so `"5"++` answers 6 while `o + 1` on the same value does something else - the silent-coercion class, filed as Cotal-AI/Cotal#646 and NOT built into the new engine. Under the mutant the operand passes through unrefused, which is the walker's answer minus even its coercion.

mutations.name: a non-function callee is called instead of refused
mutations.expectRed: calling a record is L4011
mutations.completionMarker: ok a function callee passes through as itself
mutations.cell: calling a record is L4011
mutations.note: Seam member 14, granted in ruling 1c. It is the whole of the member: the transform emits it behind a `typeof`, so nothing but the refusal ever reaches it, and a `callee` that refuses nothing is a callee that is not there.

mutations.name: a branch shares its parent's key namespace instead of opening its own
mutations.expectRed: a branch frame allocates the walker's own step keys
mutations.completionMarker: ok a constructor read as a VALUE is a function, not L2001
mutations.cell: a branch frame allocates the walker's own step keys
mutations.note: Two branches running the same named effect would race for one occurrence counter, so which arm finished first would decide which step key each got - the journal would record a different pair of keys on every run and no resume could find either. The cell compares against the oracle's own keys for the same program rather than asserting a spelling.

mutations.name: a branch shares its parent's clock
mutations.expectRed: and moves without moving the parent's
mutations.completionMarker: ok a branch inherits the clock at the fork
mutations.cell: and moves without moving the parent's
mutations.note: The recorded clocks are what decide a race: an arm advances its own past the frontier and proves it cannot win. On one shared clock a sibling's effect moves every arm, so the frontier is whatever landed last and the winner is whoever the host scheduled.

mutations.name: a branch shares its parent's cancellation signal
mutations.expectRed: cancelling a branch does not cancel the run it branched from
mutations.completionMarker: ok the join takes the branch's history
mutations.cell: cancelling a branch does not cancel the run it branched from
mutations.note: A scope cancels its LOSERS. On a shared signal the first loser cancels the run that is still waiting for the winner, so a race would end every program that used one.

mutations.name: a conclave body raises the depth like a racing branch
mutations.expectRed: and a conclave body does NOT, because it has no sibling to race
mutations.completionMarker: ok a concurrent branch raises the depth
mutations.cell: and a conclave body does NOT, because it has no sibling to race
mutations.note: A conclave opens a scope but not a race: one body, nothing running beside it, so a write from inside it is as ordered as a write anywhere else. Under the mutant L2032 refuses writes that the walker allows, and the refusal names a nondeterminism that cannot occur.

mutations.name: a child signal does not inherit a parent that is already cancelled
mutations.expectRed: a child made after the cut starts cancelled AND cut
mutations.completionMarker: ok a repeated cancellation is not a third event
mutations.cell: a child made after the cut starts cancelled AND cut
mutations.note: A nested branch launched after its parent was cut is a branch that cannot win either, and it would otherwise run - and perform - with no cancellation at all, because the parent's cancel already fired before it subscribed.

mutations.name: a child signal never subscribes to its parent
mutations.expectRed: a parent's cancellation reaches the child
mutations.completionMarker: ok a child of a live signal starts live
mutations.cell: a parent's cancellation reaches the child
mutations.note: Cancellation flows down or it does nothing: a scope cancels the arm, and the arm's own nested branches keep running and keep performing against the world.

mutations.name: a soft cancellation can never be escalated to the cut
mutations.expectRed: and the ESCALATION reaches an already-cancelled child
mutations.completionMarker: ok softly, when the parent cancelled softly
mutations.cell: and the ESCALATION reaches an already-cancelled child
mutations.note: The walker re-decides the cut when a cancelled arm's own clock lands past the frontier - measured there as an infinite pure tail burning the whole step budget and killing a run whose race had already settled ok, while a resume of the same journal returned the winner. Without the escalation the engine cannot re-decide it either. The mutant is conditioned on `first` on purpose: dropping the escalation outright also breaks the FIRST cut, so it reddened the yield-boundary cell four sections earlier and graded a rule it was not aimed at. Conditioned, it leaves a fresh cut working and removes only the escalation of a signal already cancelled softly.

mutations.name: a later cancellation overwrites the reason the branch was cancelled for
mutations.expectRed: the reason stays the FIRST one, because that is what cancelled the branch
mutations.completionMarker: ok and the ESCALATION reaches an already-cancelled child
mutations.cell: the reason stays the FIRST one, because that is what cancelled the branch
mutations.note: The reason is what the Cancelled error carries out of the branch and into the trace. An escalation is not a new reason for stopping - the branch stopped when it lost - so overwriting it makes every cut arm report the escalation instead of the loss.

mutations.name: an optional call does not short-circuit a nullish member
mutations.find: if (found.from === "own" && (found.value === null || found.value === undefined) && optional === true) {
mutations.expectRed: and so does the engine, with nothing called
mutations.completionMarker: ok the walker short-circuits an absent member
mutations.cell: and so does the engine, with nothing called
mutations.note: The whole of F6's flag. Without it `o.m?.()` on an absent member is L4011 - the answer the walker gives for a member that is PRESENT and not a function, so the program is refused for a reason that is not true of it.

mutations.name: an optional call evaluates its arguments before deciding to short-circuit
mutations.find: if (found.from === "own" && (found.value === null || found.value === undefined) && optional === true) {
mutations.replace: if (((typeof args === "function" ? args() : args), found.from === "own" && (found.value === null || found.value === undefined) && optional === true)) {
mutations.expectRed: and the engine's short-circuit never asks for its arguments
mutations.completionMarker: ok while the same argument on a PRESENT method journals its effect
mutations.cell: and the engine's short-circuit never asks for its arguments
mutations.note: The reason the optional form takes a thunk at all: measured on the walker, a short-circuited call journals NOTHING while the same argument on a present method journals a `sleep`. The mutant asks the thunk for the arguments before it decides, so their effects land in the journal and a resume of that entry replays a step the walker's run never recorded. It shares its find-string with the mutant that removes the short-circuit outright; the two replaces grade different halves of the same line.

mutations.name: an optional call accepts an argument list that has already been evaluated
mutations.expectRed: an optional call handed an ARRAY refuses, rather than short-circuiting after the fact
mutations.completionMarker: ok while a present member does ask, exactly once
mutations.cell: an optional call handed an ARRAY refuses, rather than short-circuiting after the fact
mutations.note: No silent acceptance: an array reaching this parameter means the arguments ran before the seam was entered, so the short-circuit that follows would be a lie - it returns undefined having already performed whatever the arguments performed. The refusal is loud because the emitter, not the program, is what got it wrong.

mutations.name: a short-circuited optional call still runs the chain written after it
mutations.replace: return chain === undefined ? undefined : await chain(undefined);
mutations.expectRed: the engine short-circuits the chain and never runs it
mutations.completionMarker: ok and a trailing CALL
mutations.cell: the engine short-circuits the chain and never runs it
mutations.note: `o.z?.().x` answers undefined and `o.m?.().x` on a member that RETURNED undefined refuses L4010, and both give undefined to any guard written outside the host - which is why the continuation comes here at all. Under the mutant the short-circuit runs the chain against undefined, so the first shape refuses L4010 too and a program that reads a field off an absent optional call is refused where the walker answers.

mutations.name: a call continuation is accepted without the optional flag
mutations.expectRed: a continuation without the optional flag is refused, not silently run
mutations.completionMarker: ok and a record answers the field through the chain
mutations.cell: a continuation without the optional flag is refused, not silently run
mutations.note: An ordinary call's chain is written natively, because nothing in it depends on a decision only the host made. A continuation arriving without the flag is an emitter mistake, and running it anyway would hide the mistake behind an answer that happens to be right for the shapes that do not short-circuit.
